How it affects your health, work or relationships
What you're doing to break it

model: The habit I really want to break is checking my phone in bed at night. I fell into the habit of it during the pandemic, when I was working from home and felt quite lonely. Every night I'd tell myself I was just going to check one message, and then I'd mindlessly scroll through videos for an hour or more. The problem is that it eats into my sleep. I'm supposed to be in bed by eleven, but I often don't actually fall asleep until well after one, and the next morning I feel exhausted at work. Last month I even made a silly mistake in a report because I was so tired, and my manager noticed. That was a wake-up call. I've read that you should keep your phone out of the bedroom, so I tried going cold turkey and leaving it in the kitchen. It worked for about a week, but then I slipped back into my old routine, because I use my phone as an alarm. I suppose I have no willpower late at night. So now I'm trying a more realistic approach. I've bought a cheap alarm clock, and I'm trying to cut down on screen time gradually by setting an app limit of twenty minutes after ten p.m. My sister says I ought to read a book instead, and I think she's right. If I want to feel better at work, I'd better keep going this time.
